sentences.text: Researchers developed a gold-copper cluster intended to mimic the activity of the enzyme pyruvate dehydrogenase.
In cellular settings, this material was observed to oxidize pyruvate and regenerate NAD+, a process associated with enhanced energy production and mitochondrial stability under high-sugar conditions.
When administered to diabetic mice, the cluster crossed the blood-brain barrier, a selective membrane, to influence brain energy metabolism.
The intervention activated a pathway for new mitochondria, decreased brain inflammation, and was linked to improved neurological function in these animals.
The authors suggest this approach may offer a promising direction for addressing cognitive issues arising from diabetes.
